speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I’m Dr. Agent. To help me understand your rash, can you tell me how long the itching and rash have been present and if you’ve started any new medications or products recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash have a distinct pattern, such as appearing on the elbows or knees, and have you noticed any silvery scales on the surface?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities. I also have No fever, No joint pains, No recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a personal or family history of asthma, hay fever, or eczema, and is your skin generally dry? I also need to know if the rash is symmetric and involves the flexural surfaces like the inner elbows.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No history of serious illness. No known drug allergies. Takes no medications. Social history: College student studying graphic design. Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. No recreational drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Let me examine the rash closely. I see erythematous patches with silvery scales on your extensor surfaces, particularly over the elbows. This appearance is highly characteristic of psoriasis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Psoriasis
